_readme: Races. label, age [min,max], look (image wording; null = built from the beastkin sub-type), mods (stat changes on the 0-100 scale, x10 in play: a live bonus on top of her trained stats via statBonus, not baked in, so it can exceed the cap; a 'lewd' mod is still added as-is at creation, since lewdness stays 0-100), common (false = rare/exotic), weight (odds when a generic lady is rolled), names {f,l} (optional; otherwise people.json names), needs (house upgrade id required to recruit or assign her), wage (wage multiplier), signing (signing-bonus multiplier), fx (effect engine, see traits.json _readme), client {like, dislike, classLike}.

client.like = chance per client to be an enthusiast for her race (fee x1.2, satisfaction +12). client.dislike = chance he is put off (satisfaction -15, and half the time he asks for someone else if anyone is free). classLike: extra like chance by client class.
subs (beastkin): each with weight, mods, fx and optional label/look/client/age/names that override the race's. The former dragonkin is beastkin sub 'dragon'.
Rules that are not simple numbers (demon feeding, android recharging, beastkin refusals, spirit bedlessness) live in code and read these entries.
alwaysLast: generic ladies of this race always get a last name. Beastkin subs may also set wage.
perk on a beastkin sub: {label, desc} display text for that sub's fx and wage (shown on her sheet).

design (optional, generic ladies only): skins = her skin tone is rolled from this list instead of people.json skins; builds = her build is rolled from this list; noBuilds = builds she never gets. Image looks (look) should only say what makes the race the race; height, figure, build and skin come from body.json and the design, so don't repeat them here.
